blocks.text: Dear Mr. Wagner:

Thank you for asking us to value the retiree medical plan that {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} provides to its former employees and their spouses. We appreciated the time you gave us to explain how the plan works and what the company needs from this valuation. This letter records what we agreed. It sets out the work, the people who will do it, the fee, and the terms that will govern our relationship. Please read it closely, because it is the document both of us will work from.
Scope of the Valuation

We will perform an actuarial valuation of the plan's obligation for retiree medical benefits. The valuation will cover current retirees, their covered dependents, and active employees who may become eligible for retiree coverage in the future. It will be performed as of a measurement date that we will confirm with you in writing before we request any data. The results are intended for the company's financial reporting under ASC Topic 715. They are not intended for setting retiree contributions, for budgeting, or for pricing a change to the plan, and they should not be used for those purposes without further work from us.
How We Will Go About It

We will build the valuation in the same order in which the obligation itself is built. First we gather and test the data: the census of retirees and dependents, the census of active employees, the plan document and any amendments, the summary plan description, the retiree contribution schedule, and the claims or premium history for the plan. Next we develop the expected cost of coverage at each age, which is the base for everything that follows. Only then do we set the assumptions and run the valuation.

Our report will keep three things in separate places. It will say what the data show. It will say what we assumed and why. It will say what we conclude from the two together. Where a result depends heavily on a single assumption, such as the rate at which medical costs are expected to rise, we will show how the result changes when that assumption changes.

We will perform the work in accordance with the Actuarial Standards of Practice that apply to it, among them ASOP No. 6, which addresses the measurement of retiree group benefit obligations, and ASOP No. 23, which addresses data quality. We will rely on the data and plan information that the company and its administrators provide. We will review that information for reasonableness and internal consistency, but we will not audit it. If something does not hold together, we will raise it with you before we go further.

Under the accounting standard, the assumptions are ultimately the company's. In practice we will recommend each of them to you, with one exception. The discount rate is customarily selected by management with reference to yields on high-quality corporate bonds. We will supply information to support that choice, and we will tell you if a proposed rate falls outside what we consider reasonable, but the selection belongs to the company.
Our Team

I will lead the engagement and sign the actuarial opinion. Jennifer Vasquez, Consulting Actuary, will manage the work from day to day and will be your first call on any question. Jeffrey Ochoa, Actuarial Analyst, will build the claims and cost analysis and draft the review of assumptions. Amanda White, Actuarial Associate, will prepare the exhibits and check the calculations before anything is sent to you. We will ask you to name one person at the company to coordinate data requests with us. If you would prefer to do that yourself, we are glad to work with you directly.
Fee and Start of Work

We will begin work on {{fact:f:E-2020-001.start}}. Our fee for the engagement described in this letter is fixed at {{fact:f:E-2020-001.fee}}. That fee covers the data review, the valuation, a draft report for your comments, the final report, and a meeting with you to walk through the results. If the scope changes, for example if you ask us to price a plan amendment or to value a second plan, we will tell you the cost in writing and wait for your agreement before we do the work.
We would like the data request to go out in the first days of the engagement. For that to happen, we need the following from you before work begins:

items: 1. A signed copy of this letter.
2. The name of the person who will coordinate data with us, if it is someone other than you.
3. The measurement date for the valuation and the fiscal year it supports.

4. A signed business associate agreement, which we will send under separate cover. The claims data may contain protected health information, and we will not accept a claims file until the agreement is in place.

blocks.text: Fees and Payment

We will invoice monthly for work performed. Taken together, the invoices will not exceed the fixed fee unless you have agreed in writing to a change in scope. Invoices are payable on receipt. Our ordinary expenses are included in the fee, and we do not bill separately for them.
Term and Termination

This engagement begins when you sign this letter and ends when we deliver the final report, unless one of us ends it sooner. Either of us may end it at any time by written notice to the other. If the engagement ends early, the company will pay for the work performed up to the day the notice is received, and we will return or destroy the data you provided, as you direct.
Confidentiality

We will hold the company's information, and the information about its employees, retirees and their families, in confidence. We will use it only for this engagement and will not disclose it to anyone outside our firm without your written consent, unless the law requires us to. We ask that files be sent through our secure file transfer site and not by ordinary email. Where the business associate agreement and this letter differ on the handling of health information, the agreement controls.
Reliance and Limitation of Liability

Our report will be prepared for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} and for the purpose stated in it. The company's auditors may rely on it for that purpose. No one else may rely on it without our written consent. Our total liability to the company arising from this engagement, whether in contract or otherwise, will not exceed the fees paid to us under this letter, except where the law does not permit such a limit. Neither of us will be liable to the other for lost profits or other indirect damages.
Governing Law
This letter and the work it covers are governed by the laws of the state where our principal office is located. If any provision is found to be unenforceable, the others remain in effect.
Acceptance

If this letter reflects your understanding, please sign on the line provided for the company below and return a copy to me or to Jennifer Vasquez. If anything in it differs from what you expected, please call me before you sign, and we will correct it. We look forward to working with you and your staff on this valuation.
Sincerely,

To: Jennifer Vasquez, Amanda White, Linda Hanna
From: Jeffrey Ochoa
Re: {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} retiree medical valuation, opening the work

We are ready to send the data request as soon as two administrative items clear. The engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2020-001.start}}, the signed letter is on file, and Jason Wagner, General Manager at {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}, will coordinate the data for the company himself.

Our objective is a valuation of the company's retiree medical obligation for its financial reporting. It should rest on data we have checked, plan terms we have confirmed against the documents, and assumptions we can defend one at a time. We do not yet know whether another actuary has valued this plan before. If one has, we want that report early. It gives us a point to reconcile to, and it shows us which assumptions the auditors have already seen.
Who carries what

items: 1. Data intake and checks: Amanda White. Log every file as it arrives. Run the edit checks on both censuses: missing or impossible birth dates, duplicate identifiers, retirees with no coverage election, dependents with no matching retiree. Reconcile headcounts by coverage tier to the enrollment reports. Every exception goes on the data log with its source and its resolution.

2. Plan provisions: Jeffrey Ochoa. Summarize eligibility, retiree contributions, spouse and surviving spouse coverage, and coordination with Medicare. Mark any point where the plan document and the summary plan description disagree. Those go to Jennifer before anything goes to the client.

3. Claims and cost by age: Jeffrey Ochoa. Build expected cost at each age from the claims or premium history, separately for retirees under and over Medicare age. The observed experience and the cost curve we recommend sit in separate exhibits. The first is a measurement. The second is a judgment, and it is labeled as one.

4. Assumptions: Jeffrey Ochoa, reviewed by Jennifer Vasquez. Health care cost trend, mortality, retirement, termination and election rates, plus yield information to support management's discount rate. The excise tax on high-cost coverage was repealed at the end of last year and does not belong in this measurement. If a prior valuation loaded for it, we show the difference rather than carry it.
5. Exhibits and checking: Amanda White. Build the exhibit shells now, so results go into a format that has already been reviewed. Check every calculation before it leaves the firm.
6. Administration: Linda Hanna. Business associate agreement, billing setup, and the tracker of files received and outstanding.

blocks.text: Before the request goes out

The claims files will carry protected health information, so nothing is requested until the business associate agreement is countersigned. The measurement date also has to be fixed first, because the census and the claims cutoff are both keyed to it. It will probably fall at the company's fiscal year-end. That is a likely answer, not a confirmed one, and the request does not go out on a likely answer.

items: 1. Linda Hanna: send the business associate agreement to Jason Wagner, set up billing, and open the client folder on the secure transfer site.
2. Amanda White: prepare the data request from our retiree medical checklist, trimmed to what this plan needs.
3. Jeffrey Ochoa: confirm the measurement date with Jason Wagner in writing.
4. Jennifer Vasquez: review the request before it goes to the client.

blocks.text: Once Jennifer clears the request, I will send it to Jason. From then until the files close, Amanda and I will go through the data log together each Monday, and Jennifer will get a copy of the log after each of those meetings. Questions about plan terms come to me. Questions about the files go to Amanda.
Good morning Jason,

The retiree and active census files you sent are complete, and both load cleanly. Amanda White has run our edit checks, and the headcounts by coverage tier agree with the enrollment summary for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}. Those counts are observed. Nothing in them depends on an assumption yet, which is the footing we want before we build anything on top of them.

The claims history and the plan documents are what we still need. The claims history is how we estimate the cost of coverage at each age, so the rest of the valuation waits on it. Once the files arrive, we will reconcile the claims to enrollment before we use them and send you any questions in a single list. When you can, please send:

items: Monthly paid claims for the most recent several years your administrator can provide, split between retirees under and over Medicare age, with enrollment for the same months
The current plan document and summary plan description, with any amendments
The retiree contribution schedule now in effect

blocks.text: Because the claims data carry protected health information, please use the secure transfer site rather than email. If it is simpler for your administrator to send the claims to us directly, we are glad to arrange that with them. Jennifer Vasquez and Amanda White are copied here and can answer questions about the request as well.

Thanks,
Jeffrey
{{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} retiree medical valuation. Working session held by video conference.
Present

items: Jason Wagner, General Manager, {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}
Jennifer Vasquez, Consulting Actuary
Jeffrey Ochoa, Actuarial Analyst
Amanda White, Actuarial Associate

blocks.text: Purpose
The session reviewed the completed data checks and the first look at claims experience. No assumptions were set. The aim was to agree on what the data show before the team proposes assumptions.
Census and plan terms

Amanda White reported that the census and enrollment data are closed. Every exception on the data log has been resolved with the company's staff. Jason Wagner confirmed the resolutions for retirees whose coverage elections were missing.

Jennifer Vasquez noted that the plan document and the summary plan description describe surviving spouse coverage differently. The team will value the terms in the plan document. Jason Wagner will confirm that the company administers the plan on those terms.

Jeffrey Ochoa reported that the plan document requires retirees to enroll in Medicare when they become eligible, with the plan paying secondary. The valuation will apply that rule to every retiree of Medicare age. Jason Wagner confirmed that this matches current practice.
Claims experience

Jeffrey Ochoa presented paid claims by month, split between retirees under and over Medicare age. Claims fell sharply in the spring and have recovered only in part. The likely cause is care deferred during the pandemic, but the data cannot confirm that.

Jennifer Vasquez set out the team's position. The lower months are measured experience and will be reported as such. They will not be used to reduce the expected cost of coverage, because there is no basis to assume they will persist. Some deferred care may return later as higher claims.

Jason Wagner asked whether leaving those months out overstates the obligation. Jeffrey Ochoa answered that the earlier years carry most of the weight and are consistent with one another. The report will show the effect of including the lower months in a separate exhibit.
Retiree contributions

The contribution schedule arrived after the data log closed. Jennifer Vasquez asked whether contributions are set as a share of cost or as a fixed amount. Jason Wagner said the company sets them each year and follows no formula.
How contributions are assumed to change is a judgment, and it affects the obligation directly. The team will ask for the contribution history before proposing an assumption.
Assumptions

Trend, mortality, retirement and election rates come next. Jeffrey Ochoa will draft each with the observed experience and the recommended assumption in separate columns. The discount rate remains management's selection.
Jennifer Vasquez will send Jason Wagner a short note on the bond yield information the team can provide. The note will say what the information supports and what it does not.
Actions

rows: Confirm how surviving spouse coverage is administered
Draft assumption review: trend, mortality, retirement, election
Exhibit of cost basis with and without the lower months
Check cost by age against claims totals and enrollment

blocks.text:
Prepared for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}
Prepared by Jeffrey Ochoa, Actuarial Analyst, with Jennifer Vasquez, Consulting Actuary, and Amanda White, Actuarial Associate
Where the work stands

The valuation is on schedule and within budget. The data are closed, the cost of coverage by age is developed and checked, and the draft assumptions are with Jennifer Vasquez for review. We have not yet run the valuation itself. No obligation figure exists at this stage, and none should be read into anything in this report.

Our fee remains fixed at {{fact:f:E-2020-001.fee}}. Nothing in the work so far has fallen outside the scope set out in the engagement letter, and we do not expect to ask for a change. If that view changes, we will tell you before any additional work is done.
Completed since the working session
Since we last met with your team, we have closed out the items that were holding up the cost analysis.

items: 1. Plan terms. The surviving spouse question is settled. Your staff confirmed that the plan is administered according to the plan document, and we have valued it on those terms. We suggest the summary plan description be brought into line at its next revision. That is a recommendation about the document, not a finding about the obligation.

2. Cost of coverage by age. We built the expected annual cost of coverage at each age from the claims history, separately for retirees under and over Medicare age. Amanda White checked the development against the claims totals and the enrollment counts, and the two agree.

3. Deferred care exhibit. As agreed, we prepared an exhibit showing the cost basis with and without the spring months, when claims fell. The difference is measured and labeled. It is not built into the basis we recommend.

blocks.text: What the data show and what we have assumed

We want to be plain about which parts of this work are measurement and which are judgment, because the report will draw the same line. The census, the enrollment counts and the claims history are measurements. We tested them, and they hold together.

The cost curve by age is partly judgment. The plan's own data are thin at the oldest ages, so at those ages we blended the plan's experience with published age curves. That blending is an assumption. The draft documents it, along with the effect of relying on the plan's experience alone.

Trend, mortality, retirement and election rates are judgments. Each draft assumption sits beside what the plan's data can tell us about it, and where the data cannot tell us much, the draft says so. For the long-term trend we are using the Society of Actuaries' long-run medical cost trend model, the common reference for this kind of measurement, with our own inputs set out in the draft.

One item is neither measurement nor judgment. The excise tax on high-cost coverage was repealed at the end of last year, so the valuation does not include it. That follows from the law as it stands, and we note it only so that no one looks for it in the results.
Ahead of preliminary results

Jennifer Vasquez will finish her review of the draft assumptions, and we will then send them to you with a short memo explaining each one. Once your staff have had a chance to respond, we will run the valuation and prepare preliminary results. Those results will come to you as a draft, with the main exhibits and a table showing how the obligation moves under different assumptions, before any report is final.

We will need the company's discount rate before we run the valuation, because every result depends on it. We will send you yield information on high-quality corporate bonds to support that selection. The selection itself remains with management.
Risks we are watching

items: 1. Claims after deferred care. If claims rebound above their earlier levels, the cost basis may need another look. We will review the most recent months your administrator can supply before results are final.
2. Discount rate timing. Results cannot be finalized until the company has selected its rate.

3. Plan changes. If the company is considering any change to retiree contributions or eligibility, please tell us now. A change adopted before the measurement date may need to be reflected, and pricing a change is outside the current scope.

blocks.text: Questions about this report can come to me or to Jennifer Vasquez. We appreciate the speed with which your staff at {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} have answered our data questions, which has kept the work on schedule.

Those attending

Jeffrey Ochoa, Actuarial Analyst
Amanda White, Actuarial Associate
Jason Wagner, General Manager, {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}

blocks.text: Preliminary results

Jennifer Vasquez presented preliminary results using the discount rate the company selected. The results are a draft. They are not the actuarial opinion and should not be circulated outside the company. They reflect the plan terms confirmed earlier, including the treatment of surviving spouse coverage.

Amanda White reported that the results were checked independently, from the census through to the obligation. One error in the dependent records was found and corrected before the meeting. The correction did not change any conclusion.
Sensitivity
Jeffrey Ochoa walked through the sensitivity exhibit. The obligation moves most with the trend assumption and the discount rate. Mortality has a smaller effect.

Jason Wagner asked whether the trend assumption could be lowered. Jennifer Vasquez said it could, if the company had evidence that its costs will rise more slowly than the reference model indicates. Without that evidence, the team does not recommend it.
Jason Wagner asked how much of the result rests on the months of deferred care. Jeffrey Ochoa answered that the recommended basis leaves those months out, as agreed at the earlier working session.
Jennifer Vasquez added that claims in the most recent months have moved back toward earlier levels. That observation is consistent with the choice. It does not prove it.
Contributions

The preliminary results assume retiree contributions rise with plan costs, which is what the contribution history shows. Jennifer Vasquez noted that this is an assumption drawn from past practice, not a plan term.
Jason Wagner said the company has made no decision to depart from that practice. If it does, the obligation will need to be remeasured.
Mortality

The Society of Actuaries published a new mortality improvement scale this fall. Jennifer Vasquez recommends adopting it for this measurement. Its effect will be shown on its own line in the draft report so the company and its auditors can see it.
Report and disclosure
Jason Wagner asked what the auditors will need. Jennifer Vasquez said the report will include the disclosure exhibits, the rationale for each assumption, and the statement of data reliance.
Jennifer Vasquez asked that the company's comments on the draft come back in writing. Each change to the report can then be traced to its source.
The auditors may contact the team directly once the report is final. Jason Wagner will let them know whom to call.
Follow-up

items: 1. Jason Wagner: confirm that no change to retiree contributions or eligibility has been adopted or announced for the coming plan year.
2. Jeffrey Ochoa: update the claims exhibit with the most recent months the administrator can supply.
3. Amanda White: check the disclosure exhibits against the valuation output.
4. Jennifer Vasquez: draft the report and send it to the company for comment.

blocks.text: The next session will review the draft report.
